lots.what_it_is: First World War 1916 Centenary, Battle of the Somme, coloured $10 silver proof coin in capsule, black presentation case, green outer box and matching certificate pouch. Sister issue of the Battle of Fromelles coin Gowans sold last week in identical packaging. Issuer and obverse not shown.

sold.note: same_item: close (sister issue, same series and format, different battle). AUD, no conversion. API record opened and its photo checked: same green box, pouch, case and capsule, complete. Hammer only, premium extra.

lots.guide_summary: Only one close entry survives: the Fromelles sister coin, SOLD at Gowans for $95 hammer about 9 Oct 2026. No same-item Somme sale, no UNSOLD and no usable ASKING price. Category guides at Gowans (not in the range): plain $10 silver proofs $50 to $80 hammer, unnamed coloured silver proofs $60, a 2025 C-mintmark coloured WWII proof $200. All AUD.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD entry (the Somme coin itself has no sale found), so both maximums are 0 under the rules. For reference only, if the user accepts the Fromelles sister issue as equivalent: keep would be 95 / 1.198 = 79.30, round down to $75; flip on resale $95 less 13% fees ($12.35) and $12 postage = $70.65 / 2.396 = 29.49, round down to $25. WebSearch was capped this session, so the issuer and wider market could not be checked.
lots.confidence_reason: Reverse, box and pouch read clearly, but the obverse and issuer are not shown, and the only sale is a sister issue, not the same coin. WebSearch hit the session cap, so no wider sold evidence.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped from the cited sources: Gowans 385390 ($200, 2025 C-mintmark WWII coloured proof), 399908/403074 ($60, unnamed coloured proofs), 406422 ($110, 2015 $5 triangular Anzac), 380361 ($30, 2014 folder coins) and 433855/433856/435463 ($60 to $70, Endangered Species $10). All figures were checked in the API and match, but they are different coins, so they are category guides only and set nothing. Atkinsons Bullion UK GBP 5 Somme proof: page opened, shows Out of stock and no price, and it is a different coin. Dropped. Prospect Stamps and Coins Perth Mint ANZAC Spirit: HTTP 403, no price, different coin. Dropped.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 shows the coin in a capsule inside a black hinged case with ribbon, a green 'First World War 1916 Centenary, Battle of the Somme' outer box, and a matching green pouch with a seal, probably holding the certificate. Photo 2 is a close-up of the coloured reverse (field gun, gunners, shells), legend 'FIRST WORLD WAR CENTENARY / 1916 BATTLE OF THE SOMME'. No obverse photo, so the issuing country, denomination and fineness cannot be read. Packaging matches Gowans lot 441854 (Fromelles) exactly.
lots.condition: Coin looks clean in its capsule with no visible spotting or toning. Case, box and pouch look complete and in good order. Certificate not seen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the certificate of authenticity inside the green pouch, and what issuer, denomination, fineness and mintage does it show? Is the capsule sealed, and is the obverse free of spots or milk marks?

lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD price is $80. 80 / 1.198 = 66.78, round down to $65 (all-in $77.87, below melt of about A$83.70). Flip: likely resale is about $96, which is what the $80 Gowans buyer paid all-in. Less 13% selling fees ($12.48) and $12 tracked postage leaves $71.52. 71.52 / 2.396 = 29.85, round down to $25. Flipping makes no sense next to melt. This is a bullion buy: anything near or under spot is fair.
lots.confidence_reason: The bar's markings are read clearly and there is one opened same-item SOLD entry. The other sales are different makers, and the price tracks spot silver.

lots.question_for_gowans: Is the bar still in its original factory seal, and is the reverse clean (no stamping or damage)? If unsealed, what does it weigh (should be about 31.1 g)?

lots.guide_summary: Per token, from same-item or close entries: Josephs $5 (1 SOLD), Abrahams $10 to $50 (4 SOLD incl. a halfpenny), Friedman $35 (2 SOLD, both better than this damaged piece). The range shown, A$5 to A$361, covers every surviving entry. The $361 is a UK dealer asking price (GBP 190 x 1.898), and the Wynyard $25 is an expired asking price. Summed lot value from Gowans SOLD results is roughly $50 to $95 hammer. No UNSOLD entries.
lots.working: No sale of this exact 3-token group, so the keep figure sums the lowest same-item SOLD price for each token: Josephs $5 + Abrahams $10 + Friedman $35 = $50. 50 / 1.198 = 41.74, round down to $40. The Friedman here is gouged and corroded, below the $35 comparables, so bidding a bit under $40 is sensible. Flip: likely resale about $70 (Josephs $5, Abrahams about $45, damaged Friedman about $20). Less 13% fees ($9.10) and $4 large-letter postage leaves $56.90. 56.90 / 2.396 = 23.75, round down to $20. The flip margin is thin.
lots.confidence_reason: All three tokens are read in the photos, with several opened same-item Gowans SOLD results for each type. But the lot value is a sum of single-token results, and the Friedman's damage makes its value uncertain.
lots.dropped_entries: Status International Auction 389 via NumisBids (AUD 150 Josephs pair, AUD 65 Abrahams pair): page returns HTTP 403, snippet only, about 28 months old, and two-piece lots. Dropped. Katz Auction 171 (USD 27.12 Abrahams VF): the URL given is a Museums Victoria catalogue item, not the sale, so the price is unverified. Dropped. Gowans 427374 (unnamed Tasmanian store token $30) and 425737 (unnamed 1855 Hobart Town token $30): issuer not identified, so category guides only. Dropped from the evidence. Minor: the researcher's bid count for 425737 was 3, but the API shows 4.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 (reverses and the Josephs obverse): Josephs 'NEW TOWN TOLL GATE / R. JOSEPHS' with the toll house, crisp and evenly worn. Kangaroo and emu 'TASMANIA 1855' reverse (Abrahams), good detail. 'TASMANIA 1857' seated-figure reverse (Friedman) with several dark lumps or gouges and corrosion. Photo 2: 'LEWIS ABRAHAMS DRAPER LIVERPOOL STREET HOBART TOWN' (the researcher's 'Pool St' is a misreading of Liverpool Street), 'VAN DIEMEN'S LAND 1855' Britannia (Josephs reverse), and 'I. FRIEDMAN PAWNBROKER ARGYLE STREET' with a deep gouge or deposit across the centre and pitting.
lots.condition: Josephs: fine, circulated, no obvious damage. Abrahams: fine, worn, even brown patina. Friedman: damaged on both sides, with gouges or deposits and corrosion.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are the marks on the Friedman pawnbroker token gouges or a removable deposit? Are any of the tokens holed, bent or cleaned?
